t: You're looking at Fulham Palace, a Grade I listed former bishop's palace on the north bank of the Thames. The site was a manor from Saxon times, and the bishops of London held it from the eighth century to the twentieth. It was their main residence from the eleventh century until 1973. Bishops who lived or died here include John Aylmer, Richard Gravesend, John Randolph and Charles James Blomfield. The historian Mandell Creighton died here in 1901, while serving as bishop. Today it is a museum with restored rooms, beside a large botanical garden and Bishops Park.
